activity.role: Theravada Mahavihara scholar composing the Samantapasadika Vinaya commentary
activity.notes: An author-specific inscriptional/colophon-linked scholarly anchor: Buddhaghosa says at the end of Samantapāsādikā that he composed the commentary in the twentieth and twenty-first regnal years of King Sirinivāsa, generally but provisionally identified with King Mahānāma of Sri Lanka. Converting approximate reign 409–431 gives c.429–430; the precise calendar years and identification are not certain and both bounds are explicitly APPROXIMATE. The Oxford Research Encyclopedia independently locates his main Sri Lankan Mahāvihāra scholarship and Visuddhimagga in the first half of the fifth century, but does NOT assert the Visuddhimagga itself was composed precisely in 429 or 430. This is a literary-activity point, not a royal office, a statement that the author personally ruled Anuradhapura, or an invented geographic coordinate.

sources.title: K. R. Norman (1983), Pali Literature, pp.129–130, Buddhaghosa / Samantapāsādikā
sources.citation_text: Norman explains the internal colophon at Samantapāsādikā 1415,18–20: composition during regnal years 20–21 of Sirinivāsa and qualified identity with Mahānāma (traditionally reigning 409–431); thus approximately 429–430, not an exact author lifespan.

sources.title: Norihisa Baba (2022), Buddhaghosa — Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Religion
sources.citation_text: Oxford's peer-reviewed article characterizes Buddhaghosa as a 5th-century Mahāvihāra scholar in Sri Lanka and documents personally attributable exegetical writings in the first half of the century.

sources.title: Buddhism in Sri Lanka: A Short History — Piyadassi? / Perera, Buddhist Publication Society
sources.citation_text: Perera, Buddhism in Sri Lanka: A Short History, places Buddhaghosa's Sri Lankan monastic and commentarial activity in Mahānāma's reign (c.410–432), at Anurādhapura.
